notes: §1985:VI.6.18.4 GR8 restricts each operand to the portion before the 'first occurrence of literal-2 within the content of the data item referenced by identifier-1' (b, measured from the leftmost position, not found = as if absent) and after it (c, not found = never eligible), both fixed before the first cycle. CobolInspect#Region computes the region once per operand before RunCycle's cycles and RunCycle requires a whole match inside it; at --std 85 InspectBinder#BindPhrases sets BeforeFromLeftmost (DialectBehavior.InspectBeforeFromFirstEligiblePosition starts at 2023), so BEFORE is searched from position 0 even with AFTER. Probes at 85: AYAAXAA ALL A AFTER X BEFORE Y (either order) 00 (2023: 02); AAABA ALL AA BEFORE AB 01; AFTER a delimiter found only at the last position 00; REPLACING ALL/FIRST/LEADING with BEFORE/AFTER on AXAXA XXAXA/AXQXA/AXQXA; ODO group at N=4 counts only its current length; ref-mod W5(2:4) and W5(5:1); signed S9(5) de-signed; numeric-edited; figurative SPACES/QUOTE delimiters; a second BEFORE refused COBOL2269. The witness covers T1-T9 and R1-R4.

next.reason: Amendment 2 (X3.23b-1993, pages VI-97 and VI-98) renumbered this rule (old GR7) and its references ('general rule 6' to 7); the requirement is the printed one. §1985:VI.6.18.4 GR8 a to c recur in §2023:14.9.22.4 GR9 a to c, each with a case added. a: 1985 'is first eligible to participate in matching at the leftmost character position of identifier-1', 2023 'is first eligible to participate in matching at the leftmost character position, or, if BACKWARD is specified, at the rightmost character position of identifier-1'. b: 1985 'from its leftmost character position up to, but not including, the' 'first occurrence of literal-2 within the content of the data item referenced by identifier-1', 2023 'the first character position that is eligible to participate up to, but not including, the first occurrence encountered of literal-2'. Left to right the first occurrence encountered is the first occurrence and, with BEFORE and AFTER both written (§1985:VI.6.18.3 SR4 'No more than one BEFORE phrase and one AFTER phrase can be specified'), the region is the same intersection, so every 1985 INSPECT is bounded the same; under BACKWARD the 2023 words run the region from the rightmost character position back to the occurrence first met from the right, which the 1985 word 'leftmost' does not give. c: 1985's one region, 'from the character position immediately to the right of the rightmost character position of the first occurrence of literal-2 within the content of the data item referenced by identifier-1 to the rightmost character position', is 2023 c.2 word for word; 2023 c.1 adds 'If BACKWARD is specified, the associated literal-1 or the implied operand of the CHARACTERS phrase participates only in those comparison cycles that involve that portion of the content of the data item referenced by identifier-1 from the character position immediately to the left of the leftmost character position of the first occurrence of literal-2 within the content of the data item referenced by identifier-1 to the leftmost character position'. BACKWARD is refused in 1985 (§1985:VI.6.18.2 prints identifier-1 directly after INSPECT) and accepted in 2023 (§2023:14.9.22.2 prints an optional 'BACKWARD' before identifier-1): a case added (family ruling). The earlier KEPT called the BACKWARD branches unreachable from 1985 syntax, the ground the ruling rejects. This rule's own text adds a second case: 2023 a reads 'If neither the BEFORE nor AFTER phrase is specified or identifier-4 references a zero-length item' where 1985 a reads 'If neither the BEFORE nor AFTER phrase is specified, literal-1'; 1985 has no rule for a zero-length identifier-4, which §1985:VI.6.18.3 SR2 requires to be elementary ('must reference an elementary item described, implicitly or explicitly, as USAGE IS DISPLAY') while the 1985 text names only a 'zero-length group item' (§1985:VI.6.3.1.2), and §2023:8.5.4 lists elementary ones ('A data item defined with the DYNAMIC LENGTH clause that is a zero-length item'). b and c end alike in both ('as though the BEFORE phrase had not been specified'; 'is never eligible to participate in the comparison operation'). 'to': GR9 states the whole rule; §2023:14.9.22.4 GR3 states in its own words that 'the establishment of boundaries for the BEFORE or AFTER phrase' 'begins at the leftmost character position of the data item referenced by identifier-1, regardless of its class, and proceeds from left to right to the rightmost character position'.
